comparison: Perfect agreement on epistasis experiments (C10, C90-C95). Both evaluations find the double knockout data compelling evidence for a sequential model. OpenEval emphasizes non-additive phenotypes indicating same pathway; peer reviewers highlight this as a key strength showing the proteins are not additive in their roles.

Strong agreement on Doc2α's role in asynchronous release after single stimuli (C2, C4, C30-C40, C57-C58). Both evaluations support the finding with high confidence. OpenEval emphasizes convergence across three methodologies (54-67% reduction); peer reviewers affirm Doc2α functions from initial stimulus while Syt7 does not at this early stage. Peer review includes C5 not in OpenEval result.

Divergent evaluations of mathematical modeling (C70-C88, C103-C106). OpenEval finds model SUPPORTED as proof-of-concept that mechanism is plausible, acknowledging limitations. Peer review is UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 3 questions whether modeling is necessary, Reviewer 1 cannot evaluate it. Modeling not strongly endorsed by peer reviewers despite no major concerns raised.

Agreement on background/context claims (C1, C15, C18-C29). Both evaluations support these as accurate characterization of field controversies. OpenEval notes they provide essential context but are not new findings; peer reviewers accept this framing of the controversy the study addresses.

Agreement on baseline ultrastructure findings (C54-C55). Both evaluations support that baseline synaptic structure is normal in knockouts. OpenEval emphasizes this as important control; peer reviewers accept without concern, though note caution about kinetic interpretations from EM (C56 in peer review but not OpenEval R8).

Agreement on Doc2α's fusion role vs docking (C8-C9, C64-C65, C67). Both evaluations support the dissociation between docking and release phenotypes. OpenEval emphasizes EM evidence showing normal/enhanced docking recovery with persistent release reduction; peer reviewers note this distinction is central to positive assessment, with Doc2α mutants showing facilitation and increased synchronous release.

Strong agreement on Syt7's role in vesicle docking (C3, C6, C59-C63, C66). Both evaluations support this as a novel, key finding. OpenEval emphasizes direct ultrastructural evidence with quantitative measurements; peer reviewers treat this as major contribution, with Reviewer 1 stating rapid freeze EM provides support for Syt7 in SV docking/capture. Peer review includes additional train stimulation claims (C7, C46-C47, C50-C53, C68) not in OpenEval R2.

Partial overlap on train stimulation experiments (C7, C41-C42, C45-C47, C49-C53). OpenEval R3 focuses on both Doc2α and Syt7 requirements during repetitive activity with consistent reductions across methodologies. Peer R2 emphasizes Syt7's role in supporting both synchronous and asynchronous release during trains, with docking/capture mechanism. Both support findings but with different emphasis.

Partial overlap on train dynamics characterization (C41-C42, C45). OpenEval R3 covers broader train stimulation findings including both sensors; peer R6 focuses on specific WT and mutant phenotypes during trains. Both evaluations support the data, with peer reviewers noting some phenotypes previously reported.

Agreement on spatial analysis (C48). OpenEval emphasizes this addresses confound about different bouton populations, supporting interpretation of changes at individual synapses. Peer review accepts this as part of overall train dynamics dataset without specific comment.

Agreement on Doc2α effects on paired-pulse and train dynamics (C43-C44). OpenEval notes Doc2α deletion doesn't affect initial paired-pulse but alters depression time course, consistent with model. Peer review accepts these characterizations as part of train dynamics dataset.

Partial overlap on sequential model and modeling (C11, C68-C69, C89, C103-C105). OpenEval finds sequential model well-supported by integration of data types, with modeling demonstrating plausibility despite limitations. Peer review is uncertain about modeling necessity (see R7/R5 comparison), though accepts sequential model concept.

Minimal overlap on Doc2α train phenotype (C44). OpenEval R9 focuses on paired-pulse and depression time course; peer R3 discusses Doc2α mutants showing facilitation and higher synchronous release initially. Both support findings but address different aspects.

Minimal overlap (C95). OpenEval R6 discusses overall sequential model integration; peer R4 focuses on epistasis analysis. Both support the sequential pathway concept but from different analytical perspectives.
Minimal overlap (C69). OpenEval R6 addresses sequential model broadly; peer R3 focuses on complementary roles of Doc2α vs Syt7. Both support the mechanistic framework.
Minimal overlap (C56). OpenEval R1 includes C56 in single-stimulus findings; peer R7 includes it with baseline EM observations. Both support the data.
Minimal overlap (C49). OpenEval R3 includes electrophysiology during trains broadly; peer R3 focuses on complementary roles. Both support the findings.
Minimal overlap (C68). OpenEval R6 discusses sequential model; peer R2 emphasizes Syt7 docking role during trains. Both support the mechanistic interpretation.

Minimal overlap (C106). OpenEval R11 finds catalytic model for Syt7 UNCERTAIN, noting it doesn't explain facilitation; peer R5 includes C106 in broader modeling discussion rated UNCERTAIN. Both express reservations about aspects of the model.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty about Syt7 catalytic model (C106-C109), noting it doesn't explain facilitation and alternative mechanisms remain untested. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of this limitation, though modeling generally questioned.

OpenEval supports implementation of sensor competition in model (C112-C116) with plausible molecular interpretations, while acknowledging model lumps processes together. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific modeling feature.

OpenEval supports contextual claims from recent literature (C96-C102), noting speculation about Syt7 localization is reasonable but untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific background claims.
OpenEval supports observation about experimental system limitation (C111), noting authors appropriately acknowledge it. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific limitation.

OpenEval supports contextual claims about mechanisms not explicitly modeled (C119-C120), noting they provide useful context from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific background claims.
